title: Dévissage des complexes ½ simpliciaux ∂ - parfaits et structures multiplicatives… (1975 ou 1976) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 77-80). Grothendieck works in an additive category P_1 together with groups of 'polynomial maps': P_n(X;M) are homogeneous maps of degree n, and P_alpha(X_1,...,X_r;M) are multihomogeneous maps of multidegree alpha. This is an abstract stand-in for Roby's polynomial laws. From it he wants to recover, representably:
- a tensor product, via P_1(X_1⊗...⊗X_r;M) ≅ P_{1,...,1}(X_1,...,X_r;M);
- divided powers Γ^n(X), via P_1(Γ^n X;M) ≅ P_n(X;M), with universal degree-n map γ_n: X → Γ^n X;
- multi-divided powers Γ^ν(X_1,...,X_r), representing P_ν(X_1,...,X_r;-).
The ultimate aim is to extend such functors (Γ^n, determinants, multiplicative structures) to perfect / half-simplicial complexes by dévissage.

This page:
1. For ν=(ν_1,...,ν_r), composing with the universal maps γ_{ν_i}: X_i → Γ^{ν_i}X_i gives a natural map P_{1,...,1}(Γ^{ν_1}X_1,...,Γ^{ν_r}X_r;M) → P^⊗_ν(X_1,...,X_r;M). Equivalently there is a comparison morphism Γ^ν(X_1,...,X_r) → Γ^{ν_1}X_1⊗...⊗Γ^{ν_r}X_r. Grothendieck phrases this so it also makes sense without assuming representability ('forme abstraite des questions de représentabilité', presumably working in a presheaf category). He then AXIOMATICALLY assumes this map is an isomorphism.
2. Consequence: the exponential law Γ^n(X_1×...×X_r) ≅ ⊕_{|ν|=n} Γ^{ν_1}X_1⊗...⊗Γ^{ν_r}X_r. Here × is the biproduct, and a degree-n polynomial map on a direct sum splits into its multihomogeneous components. He notes it suffices to prove the case r=2 and induct.
3. Unit: set 1 := Γ^0(0). Then X⊗1 ≅ Γ^1(X)⊗Γ^0(0) ≅ Γ^{1,0}(X,0) ≅ X, since P_{1,0}(X,0;M) = P_1(X;M); similarly 1⊗X ≅ X. This answers the previous page's question of why the unit must be Γ^0(0).
4. He then assumes tensor products are functorial and that the Γ^n satisfy the condition above.

Next page: Γ^* turns sums into ⊗. Since every object is a commutative group object for ⊕, each Γ^*(X) becomes a commutative graded ⊗-algebra. He also builds plethysm maps Γ^{pq} → Γ^pΓ^q with associativity, i.e. the divided-power-algebra structure, abstractly.
errors: No mathematical error. The key step (Γ^ν ≅ ⊗Γ^{ν_i}) is assumed as an axiom, not proved; for modules it is Roby's theorem. Without some flatness/representability hypotheses it can fail in a general additive framework, which is why he imposes it.
The decomposition of P_n on a biproduct into multihomogeneous components P_ν is used implicitly (it is part of his axioms on earlier pages).

ideas.what: Defining tensor products and divided powers representably from an abstract system of (multi)homogeneous polynomial maps on an additive category
ideas.modern_name: Categories with polynomial maps / representable 'polynomial multicategory'; close to Friedlander–Suslin's divided-power category Γ^d P and strict polynomial functors
ideas.usually_credited_to: Roby (polynomial laws, 1963); Lambek/Hermida (representable multicategories); Friedlander–Suslin 1997 (strict polynomial functors)

ideas.what: Exponential law Γ^n(X⊕Y) ≅ ⊕ Γ^p X⊗Γ^q Y, derived from the comparison Γ^ν ≅ ⊗Γ^{ν_i}
ideas.usually_credited_to: Roby 1963; Illusie (Complexe cotangent, for simplicial extensions)

ideas.what: Unit object of ⊗ obtained as Γ^0(0)
ideas.modern_name: Unit of the tensor product as degree-0 divided power

missed.claim: An axiomatic 'polynomial category' framework is sketched here. It starts from additive P_1 plus multigraded polynomial hom-groups, and from these derives ⊗, its unit, Γ^n, the exponential law and (next page) divided-power algebra and plethysm structures, all representably. The aim is to extend multiplicative functors to perfect complexes. This axiomatization was never developed or published.
missed.quote: on suppose que c'est un iso. Moyennant quoi, on a Γ^n(X_1×⋯×X_r) ≃ Σ Γ^{ν_1}(X_1)⊗⋯⊗Γ^{ν_r}(X_r)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It anticipates treating polynomial maps as primary structure from which monoidal and divided-power structure is reconstructed. This is close in spirit to strict polynomial functors and to current work on derived divided powers / derived binomial rings (Brantner–Mathew, Raksit) and to polynomial functors on additive ∞-categories. It is mainly of historical interest, as the later literature reached these ideas independently.

deep.surprise_reason: The mathematical content (exponential law, unit) is classical for modules. The abstract representable axiomatization of polynomial maps in an additive category, aimed at perfect complexes, is an unpublished framework of modest novelty, anticipating later strict-polynomial and derived divided-power viewpoints.
transcription_corrections: Line 2 likely reads 'représentabilité ... (ainsi que par les Γ^{ν_i}(X_i))', i.e. allowing non-representable Γ^{ν_i} viewed in the presheaf category.
'M dans P,' should be 'M dans P_1'.
In the exponential formula, the first X is overwritten ('X^1_1'); read Γ^n(X_1×⋯×X_r), with the sum over ν∈N^r, Σν_i=n.
'on aura une [?]' plausibly 'on aura une flèche naturelle' or similar (uncertain).
The final paragraph plausibly reads 'On suppose que les produits tensoriels sont définis et fonctoriels / forment des foncteurs, et que l'on a des Γ^nX satisfaisant à la condition plus haut'.
